page: Amazon Web Services g5.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server designed for graphics-intensive and parallel computing workloads. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs, corresponding to 48 physical cores, powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance bundles four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs with a combined VRAM of 89 GB. For local storage, it includes 3800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps, facilitating rapid data transfers for distributed tasks.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks, achieving top 10% scores in prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models. Ray tracing and image processing benchmarks register as strong, reflecting the capabilities of the Ampere GPUs. While single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth are average, and CPU encryption tests rank in the top 10%.

Given the high density of four dedicated GPUs, 384 GB of RAM, and 3.8 TB of fast NVMe storage, this instance offers a specialized hardware profile optimized for parallel processing. It is highly suited for large language model inference, real-time ray tracing, image processing, and cryptography-heavy applications, though it presents a single-core performance tradeoff.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive and parallel computing workloads. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, it integrates four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs with 89 GB of total VRAM. The server also features 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight top-tier performance in large language model inference across various model sizes, alongside strong results in ray tracing, image processing, and CPU encryption. While single-core CPU performance is a notable tradeoff, its multi-core capabilities and massive GPU resources make it highly efficient for machine learning deployment, rendering, and cryptographic tasks.
